date_note: Date is the PIPC warning of 24 November as reported by Newsis; the page gives no earlier day.
title: Korea's PIPC warns of phishing emails impersonating the commission with fake breach notices
summary: Newsis reports that the Personal Information Protection Commission warned on 24 November of emails sent in its name that tell recipients their personal data may have leaked and urge them to open a PDF attachment. The commission says the sender domain differed from its official korea.kr and that any breach notice sent under its staff's name should be treated as malicious.
plain: Fake emails posing as Korea's privacy regulator claim your data leaked and push an attachment. The regulator says its real notices do not come this way.
exec: Phishing posing as a regulator's breach notice can lead to stolen logins or malware.
action: The PIPC advises checking the sender's domain, not opening attachments or links, refusing remote-control app requests, and reporting to police or the Personal Information Infringement Report Center.

validation.note: Only Newsis read, quoting the PIPC's warning; the PIPC's own page was not read.
